item.title: [44★] A modular quantum computer based on Cornucopia codes
item.author: Zhide Lu, ..., Zheng-Zhi Sun, Dong-Ling Deng
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 44 ★

Authors: Zhide Lu, ..., Zheng-Zhi Sun, Dong-Ling Deng

arXiv ID: 2610.19073 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Ultra-high-rate quantum error correction codes can store many logical qubits in a single code block with few physical qubits. A fault-tolerant quantum computer, however, also requires a universal set of logical operations on individually addressable logical qubits, and the ancilla overhead of these operations may erode the advantage of the high encoding rate. Here, we propose the Cornucopia architecture, in which a universal set of logical operations is implemented at low overhead for the Cornucopia codes. In particular, we focus on the [[2844,1426,18]] Cornucopia code as an example and introduce a modular quantum computer built from such code blocks connected by bridges. Each block stores 1,426 logical qubits and serves as a universal logical processor. Exploiting the code's translation symmetry, we construct a family of reusable gadgets that individually address 1,422 logical qubits within each block. These gadgets support three universal logical instruction sets: basic, high-throughput and fixed-extractor. Excluding magic-state factories, a module with sufficient workspace to execute any instruction in the basic set requires an average of 4.1 physical qubits per logical qubit, compared with 3.0 for memory alone. The architecture thus preserves the resource advantage of ultra-high-rate quantum memory while enabling universal logical computation, providing a route towards low-overhead fault-tolerant quantum computers.

Zhide Lu, ..., Zheng-Zhi Sun, Dong-Ling Deng

item.title: [43★] Logical CCZ state cultivation
item.author: Yuta Hirasaki, Jong Yeon Lee
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 43 ★

Authors: Yuta Hirasaki, Jong Yeon Lee

arXiv ID: 2610.20591 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Logical CCZ states enable Toffoli gates, a central building block of fault-tolerant quantum arithmetic. We introduce an end-to-end protocol for direct CCZ-state preparation on bivariate tricycle and bicycle (BT/BB) codes. Our factory combines the cup-product CCZ gates native to BT codes with two novel ingredients, both enabled by engineering the logical coupling between BT and BB codes through projection-preserving lifts. Index-2 lifted BB ancillas enable selective ZZZ-basis initialization, allowing the native cup-product gates to directly prepare two disjoint logical CCZ states. The prepared CCZ states are faithfully transferred to index-3 lifted BB memories with high code distance. We use decoder-based postselection to obtain high-fidelity output states with low overhead. We perform exact simulations of our factory under a circuit-level noise model motivated by neutral-atom hardware, obtaining joint infidelities of 1.84×10−51.84×10−51.84\times10^{-5} at 21.94%21.94%21.94\% acceptance and 4.10×10−74.10×10−74.10\times10^{-7} at 8.89%8.89%8.89\% acceptance for single-qubit, CZ, and CCZ error rates of 0.01%0.01%0.01\%, 0.1%0.1%0.1\%, and 0.5%0.5%0.5\%, respectively. At the output-infidelity target of our smallest factory, its estimated spacetime cost per CCZ state is lower than that of TTT-state cultivation followed by CCZ conversion, providing an efficient route to logical CCZ states for fault-tolerant quantum computation.

Yuta Hirasaki, Jong Yeon Lee

item.title: [32★] Logical gate set tomography
item.author: Piper C. Wysocki, ..., Charles H. Baldwin, Kenneth M. Rudinger
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 32 ★

Authors: Piper C. Wysocki, ..., Charles H. Baldwin, Kenneth M. Rudinger

arXiv ID: 2610.19034 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Quantum error correction (QEC) can strongly suppress noise, but predicting whether a computation succeeds requires understanding not only how much effective noise persists after QEC, but what form that noise takes. To thoroughly characterize this noise, we introduce logical gate set tomography (``logical GST''). Logical GST produces detailed representations of noisy logical operations that can be used to derive higher-level metrics, such as gate fidelity and diamond distance, and to test for non-Markovian and coherent logical errors. We use logical GST to obtain the first full, self-consistent characterization of a universal single-qubit logical gate set, implemented in the seven-qubit Steane code using Quantinuum System Model H1, a 20-qubit trapped-ion quantum processor. In the experimental data from H1, logical GST identified predominantly logical Pauli-stochastic errors, found no evidence of logical non-Markovianity, and detected weak potential signatures of coherent logical error. By contrast, higher-shot datasets generated with Quantinuum's detailed system emulator, identify mechanisms for weak but statistically significant logical non-Markovianity and strong evidence of coherent logical error. Finally, we use logical GST to perform error attribution with the system emulator, revealing how specific physical error sources shape logical error mechanisms.

Piper C. Wysocki, ..., Charles H. Baldwin, Kenneth M. Rudinger

item.title: [19★] Testing graph isomorphism using simple quantum circuits
item.author: Samuel Beasley, Ashley Montanaro
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 19 ★

Authors: Samuel Beasley, Ashley Montanaro

arXiv ID: 2610.19962 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

The graph isomorphism problem asks whether two graphs are equivalent up to a permutation of their vertices. Its precise computational complexity remains unresolved, and it is still unknown whether a polynomial-time algorithm exists. We investigate whether simple graph-dependent Instantaneous Quantum Polynomial-time (IQP) and Quantum Approximate Optimisation Algorithm (QAOA) circuits can distinguish non-isomorphic graphs. We first show that suitable IQP and QAOA constructions allow the underlying graph to be reconstructed using a polynomial number of samples. Building on previous work using the QAOA energy, we show that Hamming weight distributions can distinguish graph pairs at circuit depths for which the numerically computed energy gap is zero. We then apply graph invariants to the matrix of ZZ correlators on the output distribution. For the specific case of the graph spectrum, at QAOA depth p=2p=2p=2, this invariant numerically distinguishes all 10,48610,48610{,}486 cospectral regular graph pairs tested on up to 18 vertices. For IQP circuits, we introduce a finer invariant based on probability multiplicities within Hamming weight sectors, which distinguishes every non-isomorphic graph pair tested numerically. Finally, we derive exact graph-theoretic characterisations of the IQP output distribution at θ=π/2θ=π/2\theta=\pi/2 and θ=π/4θ=π/4\theta=\pi/4. These results show that simple graph-dependent quantum circuits encode substantial structural information, while leaving open whether this information can be extracted efficiently for general graph isomorphism.

Samuel Beasley, Ashley Montanaro

item.title: [14★] Gap-Priced |T⟩|T⟩|T\rangle-States: Dynamic |T⟩|T⟩|T\rangle Post-Selection and Budget-Aware Factory Provisioning
item.author: Maxwell Poster, ..., Jonathan Baker, Costin Iancu
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 14 ★

Authors: Maxwell Poster, ..., Jonathan Baker, Costin Iancu

arXiv ID: 2610.19299 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Magic |T⟩|T⟩|T\rangle-state preparation dominates the cost of fault-tolerant quantum computation on surface codes, yet cultivation and distillation are typically provisioned statically, leaving much of the program's error budget unused. We present Gap-Priced |T⟩|T⟩|T\rangle States (GP|T⟩|T⟩|T\rangle-S), a lattice surgery scheduler and factory allocator that co-optimizes both methods under a total TTT-error budget. GP|T⟩|T⟩|T\rangle-S uses the complementary gap of each cultivated state as a fidelity estimate and dynamically adjusts the cultivation gap cutoff, converting budget slack into speed by giving the scheduler control over the cultivation post-selection. GP|T⟩|T⟩|T\rangle-S also characterizes distillation factories by size, |T⟩|T⟩|T\rangle-state production rate, and budget slack, and introduces cultivating factories that embed cultivation within routing channels, achieving fidelities otherwise requiring two-level distillation at a single-level footprint. GP|T⟩|T⟩|T\rangle-S organizes these characterizations into a factory catalog, and performs distillation factory allocation over this catalog in tandem with the gap cutoff using dynamic-programming to achieve one of i) minimum spacetime volume, ii) minimum execution time, or iii) minimum space overhead, all within a user-provided TTT-error budget. Across sixteen benchmarks under high and low TTT-error budgets of 10−310−310^{-3} and 10−510−510^{-5} respectively, GP|T⟩|T⟩|T\rangle-S consistently outperforms cultivation-only and single-factory baselines without exceeding the budget, achieving a 5.5××\times geometric mean speedup in logical cycle count and a 3.4××\times geometric mean reduction in space-time volume.

Maxwell Poster, ..., Jonathan Baker, Costin Iancu

item.title: [14★] Instability of Markov chains under infinitesimal coherent dissipation
item.author: Amir-Reza Negari, Yijian Zou, Timothy H. Hsieh
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 14 ★

Authors: Amir-Reza Negari, Yijian Zou, Timothy H. Hsieh

arXiv ID: 2610.18983 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Under local Lindbladian evolution, the growth of conditional mutual information and its associated Markov length scale is not limited by Lieb-Robinson bounds, yet it has been unclear how quickly the Markov length can increase. We show that an arbitrarily short, strictly local Lindbladian can generate infinite Markov length from a product state. We also construct strictly local Lindbladians that converge rapidly to steady states with algebraically decaying conditional mutual information. Despite their long-range conditional correlations, the states we construct are local reversibly connected to a product state by sublinear depth circuits. Thus infinite Markov length does not imply slow relaxation nor obstruct phase stability when suitably defined.

Amir-Reza Negari, Yijian Zou, Timothy H. Hsieh

item.title: [13★] Leakage benchmarking with decohering subgroups in the presence of preparation and measurement errors
item.author: Shawn Geller, ..., Raymond W. Simmonds, Emanuel Knill
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 13 ★

Authors: Shawn Geller, ..., Raymond W. Simmonds, Emanuel Knill

arXiv ID: 2610.19304 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

A common problem with physical qubits is that the state can leak outside the computational subspace. To characterize the problem, it is desirable to measure both the leakage probability and the fidelity of gates inside the computational subspace. Randomized benchmarking is a readily accessible method for estimating average gate fidelities and can be modified to account for leakage. However, in the presence of state preparation and measurement errors (SPAM) there are parameter degeneracies, and fidelities and leakage become underdetermined. We study the example of qudits with any number of leakage levels under the assumption of gate-independent noise. We show that randomized benchmarking sequences with leakage level decoherence can be analyzed as a Markov process with noisy classical preparations and measurements. This result generalizes to randomized benchmarking with random gates from an arbitrary group that contains a phase-decohering subgroup. We characterize the parameter degeneracy in inferring the Markov process, preparations and measurements. Based on this characterization we develop a measurement and inference method taking advantage of known conservative bounds on SPAM to constrain fidelity, leakage and other parameters of the Markov process, state preparations and measurements. As part of our study, we experimentally implemented the measurement method for a qubit defined on the one-excitation subspace of two transmons, for which there are two leakage levels. We determined confidence intervals accounting for parameter degeneracy for a number of performance parameters of the system. For leakage and fidelity, we compare these intervals to those obtained for several conventional methods for leakage benchmarking.

Shawn Geller, ..., Raymond W. Simmonds, Emanuel Knill

item.title: [9★] The cost of classically simulating quantum communication is as high as it could be
item.author: Riccardo Castellano, Pavel Sekatski, Nicolas Brunner
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 9 ★

Authors: Riccardo Castellano, Pavel Sekatski, Nicolas Brunner

arXiv ID: 2610.19060 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

A long-standing open question is to characterize the classical communication cost of simulating the correlations arising from measurements on finite-dimensional quantum systems. We consider this question in the prepare-and-measure scenario. First we construct a classical simulation model involving a finite average number of bits of one-way communication that simulates exactly the correlations arising from arbitrary ddd-dimensional quantum states and arbitrary measurements. Second, we show that no classical simulation protocol involving a finite average message dimension can exist for d≥4d≥4d\geq 4, hence strengthening a recent result of de Gois, Santos and Vieira. Our first result relies on a more general simulation theorem which can be applied to certain continuous variable (i.e. infinite-dimensional) quantum systems, and even beyond quantum theory, e.g. to generalized probabilistic theories. In particular, we show that multimode Gaussian states of bounded average energy and general Gaussian measurements admit an exact classical simulation with a finite expected number of bits. Overall, our results show that the classical simulation cost of quantum communication is essentially as high as it could be.

Riccardo Castellano, Pavel Sekatski, Nicolas Brunner

item.title: [9★] Invertible subalgebras for chiral semion topological order
item.author: Yu-An Chen, ..., Zongyuan Wang, Bowen Yang
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 9 ★

Authors: Yu-An Chen, ..., Zongyuan Wang, Bowen Yang

arXiv ID: 2610.18953 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Chiral topological order is incompatible with strictly two-dimensional local commuting-projector Hamiltonians on finite-dimensional tensor-product Hilbert spaces. Invertible subalgebras (ISAs) provide an alternative framework. We construct an ISA supporting chiral semions, together with its anti-semion commutant, on a square lattice with one qubit per edge. We give explicit non-Pauli generators for both algebras and prove that together they generate all local operators on the Hilbert space. Starting from the Z4Z4\mathbb{Z}_4 toric code, we condense the boson e2m2e2m2e^2m^2 and identify the semion and anti-semion algebras. We then decompose each Z4Z4\mathbb{Z}_4 qudit into two qubits and use a finite-depth circuit to disentangle one qubit per edge fixed by the condensation constraints. Pumping the semion ISA along the zzz direction defines an explicit three-dimensional non-Clifford quantum cellular automaton (QCA). We show that pumping eight times is equivalent to a translation followed by a finite-depth quantum circuit with ancillary qubits. We also give an explicit finite-depth circuit relating this construction to the semion QCA previously obtained from topological quantum field theory. A similar condensation construction yields a U(1)4U(1)4U(1)_4 ISA on a square lattice. Together with the semion and earlier odd-prime ISAs, finite stacking realizes every pointed Witt class of bosonic Abelian anyon theories. Finally, we extend both constructions to all spatial dimensions d=4k−2d=4k−2d=4k{-}2, with one qubit or Z4Z4\mathbb{Z}_4 qudit on each (2k−1)(2k−1)(2k{-}1)-cell for the semion or U(1)4U(1)4U(1)_4 ISA, respectively.

Yu-An Chen, ..., Zongyuan Wang, Bowen Yang

item.title: [8★] Measurement-induced criticality for non-Abelian anyons: The monitored golden chain
item.author: Zhaohui Zhi, ..., Simon Trebst, Guo-Yi Zhu
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 8 ★

Authors: Zhaohui Zhi, ..., Simon Trebst, Guo-Yi Zhu

arXiv ID: 2610.18965 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Non-Abelian anyon chains whose interactions favor a single fusion channel host quantum critical ground states described by minimal-model conformal field theories (CFTs) protected by a topological symmetry. We show that their measurement-only counterpart, where non-commuting fusion charge measurements act locally on the anyons of a chain of LLL sites, provides a fundamental example of a non-unitary CFT controlling a non-Abelian learning problem. Mapping the monitored dynamics to a random tensor network, we numerically find 1/L1/L1/L scaling Lyapunov gaps, logarithmic entanglement scaling with the chord length, and an effective central charge in the Shannon entropy of the measurement record. The conserved topological charge sharpens with dynamical exponent z=1z=1z= 1 and is learnable by a decoder on an O(L)O(L)O(L) time scale. As the topological symmetry is a non-invertible symmetry of the SU(2)kSU(2)kSU(2)_k anyon theories, we establish the monitored golden chain (k=3)(k=3)(k=3) as a non-Abelian generalization of the weakly (Kramers-Wannier) self-dual quantum critical point of the toric code (k=2)(k=2)(k=2), and the first of a family for k≥3k≥3k\geq 3.

Zhaohui Zhi, ..., Simon Trebst, Guo-Yi Zhu

item.title: [6★] Quantum Work Statistics from Entanglement-Assisted Invariance
item.author: Akira Sone, ..., Emery Doucet, Sebastian Deffner
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 6 ★

Authors: Akira Sone, ..., Emery Doucet, Sebastian Deffner

arXiv ID: 2610.20528 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We demonstrate that the one-time measurement scheme is more consistent than the standard two-time measurement scheme with respect to the fundamental symmetry of entanglement, namely entanglement-assisted invariance (envariance). In particular, the work statistics obtained from the one-time measurement scheme arise naturally as a direct consequence of envariance for any driving unitary, without involving an explicit measurement postulate, whereas the analogous identification for the two-time measurement scheme is possible only for a Haar-measure-zero set of unitaries. This envariance-based formulation eliminates the ambiguity in work statistics related to the energetic cost of measurement.

Akira Sone, ..., Emery Doucet, Sebastian Deffner

item.title: [6★] Quantum LDPC Codes from Polynomial Minors
item.author: Vahid Nourozi, Roxana Smarandache, David G. M. Mitchell
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 6 ★

Authors: Vahid Nourozi, Roxana Smarandache, David G. M. Mitchell

arXiv ID: 2610.19459 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We construct quantum codes from codewords of a cyclic code and the minors of a polynomial matrix. The construction uses a two-row, three-column matrix whose minors yield a second matrix satisfying the CSS orthogonality condition. We derive the code dimension from the greatest common divisors of the entries and minors, with a simplified formula for odd lifting factors. A residue characterization identifies additional common factors of the minors and leads to a method for controlling the dimension through polynomial selection. We also give a condition for changing the minor generator without changing the code. Explicit polynomial constructions yield 13 quantum codes with verified minimum distances, including a [[255,80,12]][[255,80,12]][[255,80,12]] code of rate 80/25580/25580/255.

Vahid Nourozi, Roxana Smarandache, David G. M. Mitchell

item.title: [5★] Petz Recovery through a Single Polar Transformation for Approximate Quantum Error Correction
item.author: Hanzhang Zhao, Shenglong Xu
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 5 ★

Authors: Hanzhang Zhao, Shenglong Xu

arXiv ID: 2610.20515 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

The Petz recovery map provides a near optimal decoder for approximate quantum error correction, but its inverse square-root normalization complicates circuit implementation. We use the polar structure of the Petz recovery isometry to implement recovery through a single quantum singular value transformation (QSVT). We give explicit block-encoding circuits and an extended recovery isometry that yields approximate Petz recovery without postselection. We bound the diamond distance between the approximate and ideal Petz encoding-recovery channels in terms of a spectrum-weighted loss, which provides a channel specific objective for optimizing the QSVT angles. Uniform polynomial approximation yields an asymptotic error bound that decays exponentially with the number of QSVT iterations, at a rate controlled by the smallest nonzero scaled singular value. Applications to Haar-random encoding and the Hayden-Preskill protocol illustrate the tradeoff between circuit depth and recovery accuracy and place existing scrambling decoders within a common Petz recovery framework.

Hanzhang Zhao, Shenglong Xu

item.title: [5★] Quantum Spectral Estimation with Multiple Initial States: Improved Error and Cost Scaling
item.author: Lingwei Zhang, Zhiyan Ding
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 5 ★

Authors: Lingwei Zhang, Zhiyan Ding

arXiv ID: 2610.20482 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We study quantum spectrum and eigenstate property estimation using multiple initial states and generalized Hadamard tests. Building on the QFAMES (quantum filtering and analysis of multiplicities in eigenvalue spectra) framework, we introduce a new method that samples evolution times independently for each initial-state pair. Under the stated assumptions, when statistical error determines the sampling cost, the total Hamiltonian simulation cost required for fixed-accuracy eigenvalue and observable estimation is independent of the number of initial states, up to logarithmic factors. This improves scalability when many initial states are needed to explore the target eigenspaces. The method also reduces the cost of multiplicity recovery and retains Heisenberg-limited scaling for eigenvalue estimation. Numerical experiments support the predicted statistical error scalings.

Lingwei Zhang, Zhiyan Ding

item.title: [5★] Improved Quantum Algorithms for Rényi Entropies Estimation
item.author: Zongxing Xiong, Chengshen Gao, Lvzhou Li
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 5 ★

Authors: Zongxing Xiong, Chengshen Gao, Lvzhou Li

arXiv ID: 2610.19936 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Entropy estimation of discrete probability distributions is a fundamental problem in statistical inference and quantum property estimation. In this paper, we study the problem of estimating Rényi entropy Hα(p)H_\alpha(\mathbf{p}) for any distribution p=(pi)ni=1\mathbf{p} = (p_i)_{i=1}^n given its purified quantum query-access. For non-integer α>1\alpha > 1, our algorithm estimates Hα(p)H_\alpha(\mathbf{p}) to within additive error ϵ\epsilon using only ˜O(nmax{1/2,1−1/α}/ϵ)\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\big(n^{\max\{1/2,1-1/\alpha\}}/\epsilon\big) queries, which improves the best known upper bound for dependence on both nn and 1/ϵ1/\epsilon. For 0<α<10<\alpha<1, our algorithm has query complexity ˜O(n1/(2α)/ϵmax{1,1/(2α)})\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\big(n^{1/(2\alpha)}/\epsilon^{\max\{1,1/(2\alpha)\}}\big), which improves the dependence on 1/ϵ1/\epsilon of the current best upper bound without incresing its nn dependence. Our approach adapts the multi-level estimation framework to relative approximation of the power sums and leverage binary search to remove the requirement of prior knowledge of them. We also strengthen the precision-dependent lower bound to Ω(1/ϵmax{1,1/(2α)})\Omega\big(1/\epsilon^{\max\{1,1/(2\alpha)\}}\big) for 0<α<10<\alpha<1, which identifies the optimal precision dependence of our algorithm.

Zongxing Xiong, Chengshen Gao, Lvzhou Li

item.title: [4★] Degeneracy graph determinants and higher-dimensional Young diagrams
item.author: Sanjaye Ramgoolam, Michał Studziński
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 4 ★

Authors: Sanjaye Ramgoolam, Michał Studziński

arXiv ID: 2610.20368 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Kemp and Ramgoolam proposed a basis of monomials for a commutative semisimple algebra with generators C1,…,CLC_1,\ldots, C_L, constructed from a degeneracy graph which records how the eigenspaces of C1 C_1are successively split by C2,…,CL C_2,\ldots, C_L. They showed that the basis property is equivalent to the non-vanishing of the determinant of the matrix of values of these monomials on the projector basis, and conjectured a factorised formula for this determinant, as a product of powers of eigenvalue differences. We prove this formula for any number of generators. The proof uses graph analogues of Newton polynomials. Their evaluation matrix is not triangular in general, but expanding the rows of the children of each node of the penultimate layer in a Newton basis of their eigenvalues makes it block triangular, with diagonal blocks given by smaller degeneracy graphs in which the final layer is removed. The formula then follows by induction on the number of layers. We show that the exponents in the determinant are overlap volumes of higher-dimensional Young diagrams attached to the nodes of the graph: intervals, ordinary Young diagrams, plane partitions and their higher analogues. Finally, the block triangular structure gives an explicit recursive inversion of the evaluation matrix, expressing the projectors in the monomial basis.

Sanjaye Ramgoolam, Michał Studziński

item.title: [3★] Tomography for coherent noise
item.author: Long Huang
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 3 ★

Authors: Long Huang

arXiv ID: 2610.19779 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Coherent noise poses a fundamentally greater challenge to quantum error correction than independent s- tochastic Pauli errors, because unitary errors preserve interference between error paths, can accumulate over multiple quantum error correction rounds, and leave the encoded logical channel with a residual coherent com- ponent. If the parameters of such coherent noise can be accurately determined, this knowledge can be exploited to inject correlated priors into the decoding graph, and to perform maximum-likelihood decoding under poly- nomially tractable structures, significantly improving the accuracy of syndrome-based decoding. In this work, we introduce one protocol to determine the model and parameters of coherent noise, and reduce the complexity of the experiment from 16nto O(16), which is of great significance for correcting coherent noise in quantum error correction.

Long Huang

item.title: [3★] Cavity-assisted dynamic nuclear polarisation
item.author: Tristan Lorriaux, ..., Benjamin Huard, Audrey Bienfait
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 3 ★

Authors: Tristan Lorriaux, ..., Benjamin Huard, Audrey Bienfait

arXiv ID: 2610.19180 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Dynamic nuclear polarisation transfers polarisation from electron to nuclear spins by relying on a dissipative channel. Here we introduce a cavity-based DNP mechanism which uses the radiative relaxation of the electronic spin through the Purcell effect to bring about the nuclear spin polarisation. We implement this protocol on an ensemble of bismuth donor spins (I=9/2, S=1/2) in isotopically purified silicon coupled to a superconducting resonator. A single cycle, combining adiabatic microwave and radio-frequency pulses with Purcell relaxation, increases a target ground state's population by a factor of 1.79±0.041.79\pm0.04; a cumulative enhancement of 4.6±0.24.6\pm0.2 is reached with additional cycles, to be compared with the theoretical limit of ninefold set by the degeneracy of the ground manifold. We explain this difference by the competition between Purcell and intrinsic relaxation on the one hand and a collective effect that slows down the electronic spin radiative decay as the nuclear spin population grows on the other hand. Our results place radiative DNP as an available mechanism at millikelvin temperatures where phonon-mediated relaxation is frozen.

Tristan Lorriaux, ..., Benjamin Huard, Audrey Bienfait

item.title: [2★] Dynamical Decoupling of Nonclassical States in a Biased-Noise Spin Qudit
item.author: Arjen Vaartjes, ..., David N. Jamieson, Andrea Morello
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Arjen Vaartjes, ..., David N. Jamieson, Andrea Morello

arXiv ID: 2610.19676 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Encoding quantum information in dd-dimensional systems (qudits) with d>2d>2 offers appealing new directions for resource-efficient quantum computing. However, protecting the coherence of nonclassical qudit resource states remains an open challenge. Dynamical decoupling (DD) is a well-established technique for extending coherence, but its application to qudits is hindered by the quadratic scaling of the decoupling sequence overhead with the dimension dd. As a result, demonstrations of qudit DD have so far been limited to low-dimensional qudits. Here, we show that noise-biased qudits enable a nontrivial reduction of this overhead, for example, from quadratic to linear. We perform qudit DD on a model d=8d=8 qudit, the nuclear spin of an antimony donor in silicon. We benchmark DD performance on highly nonclassical states such as uniform superpositions, cat states, and Haar random states and measure coherence improvements up to a factor 55 to 1010. For a spin-cat error correction code, continuous DD extends the coherence time of the logical superposition |+⟩L|+\rangle_L to 225225~ms, compared to 1919~ms under free evolution and 8585~ms with a Hahn echo. This improvement shows that DD sequences tailored to a system's noise bias can significantly enhance the lifetime of encoded logical qubits.

Arjen Vaartjes, ..., David N. Jamieson, Andrea Morello

item.title: [2★] Optimal Disorder Strength for Approximate Unitary kk-Designs in Spin Chains
item.author: Tian-Gang Zhou, ..., Thierry Giamarchi, Julian Sonner
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Tian-Gang Zhou, ..., Thierry Giamarchi, Julian Sonner

arXiv ID: 2610.18954 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Quantum simulators with disordered spin Hamiltonians offer a natural route to Haar-like unitary ensembles, but face a competition. Disorder enhances randomness, yet strong disorder suppresses dynamics and localizes the system in the computational basis. This suggests an optimal intermediate disorder strength for approximating a unitary kk-design, which has so far been identified mainly empirically. Here, we develop a perturbative theory for the moment gap Δ(k)\Delta^{(k)}, the deviation of the kk-th moment operator from its Haar value, for the full spectrum of the interacting XXZ chain in a fixed-magnetization sector. We find the non-monotonic asymptotic scalings lnΔ(k)∼−σ2\ln \Delta^{(k)}\sim -\sigma^2 at weak disorder and lnΔ(k)∼−1/σ\ln \Delta^{(k)}\sim -1/\sigma at strong disorder, whose crossover sets an optimal disorder strength σc∼Jxy\sigma_c\sim J_{xy}, where JxyJ_{xy} is the energy scale of the non-random interaction. We further show that a multi-quench protocol further suppresses the gap exponentially in the number of quenches. Numerical simulations confirm both scalings and this exponential suppression, and we demonstrate the usefulness of the protocol for classical shadow tomography. This work suggests that strong disorder may block both thermalization and the formation of unitary designs through a common localization mechanism.

Tian-Gang Zhou, ..., Thierry Giamarchi, Julian Sonner

item.title: [1★] Demonstration of a mobile ion-trap quantum device
item.author: Sara Alfaro, ..., Rainer Blatt, Giovanni Cerchiari
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Sara Alfaro, ..., Rainer Blatt, Giovanni Cerchiari

arXiv ID: 2610.20487 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Trapped-ion devices are being investigated for transportable applications, including the transfer of exotic charged particles between laboratories and the development of portable quantum technologies. To date, ion transport has been demonstrated only in magnetic (Penning) traps, whereas radiofrequency (Paul) traps are the predominant platform in quantum science. Here, we report the first transport of a few thousand ions confined in a linear Paul trap over distances of several kilometers, with transport durations of 15 and 45 min. These results establish a foundation for mobile trapped-ion quantum devices capable of operating while in motion and may enable the transport of exotic ions in Paul traps between experimental facilities.

item.title: [1★] Gaussian and Qubit Semigroup Dynamics beyond GKSL
item.author: Nadine Diesel, Charlotte Bäcker, Walter T. Strunz
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Nadine Diesel, Charlotte Bäcker, Walter T. Strunz

arXiv ID: 2610.20258 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

A well established approach to describe open quantum system dynamics is the celebrated Gorini-Kossakowski-Sudarshan-Lindblad (GKSL) master equation. In this article we aim to shed light on semigroup dynamics that are not of this form. Such dynamics may appear in real physical systems describing asymptotic long-time dynamics. Thus, they correspond to semigroup dynamics applicable to a restricted set of initial states only. As a way of motivating our studies, first we review known results about the single-mode Gaussian Quantum Brownian motion channel and corresponding master equations. Next we discuss a conceptually simpler family of qubit semigroup generators and identify parameter regions of completely positive, merely positive, and non-positive dynamics. We then focus on the latter case to which we will refer to as restricted-positive, as the semigroup generator may well be physically meaningful when applied to a restricted set of admissible initial states.

Nadine Diesel, Charlotte Bäcker, Walter T. Strunz

item.title: [1★] Loss-Tolerant Measurement-Device-Independent QKD over Untrusted Repeaters via High-Dimensional Time-Bin Multiplexing
item.author: Yu-Chun Yin, Ching-Yi Lai, Alexei Ashikhmin
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Yu-Chun Yin, Ching-Yi Lai, Alexei Ashikhmin

arXiv ID: 2610.20148 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We propose a loss-tolerant measurement-device-independent quantum key distribution (MDI-QKD) protocol using time-bin-multiplexed single photons entangled with local qubits stored in nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers. In each round, Alice and Bob each send a single multiplexed photon to an untrusted intermediary, Charlie. Each photon first becomes entangled with Charlie's NV-center qubits; Charlie then performs entanglement swapping between his NV qubits to establish EPR pairs between Alice's and Bob's local qubits. With dd time bins per photon, log2d+1\log_2 d + 1 EPR pairs can be generated per transmitted photon, substantially increasing the probability of EPR-pair creation under limited channel bandwidth. To further mitigate the effects of prolonged memory storage, the protocol employs a memory-insensitive (MI) architecture, where multiple banks of qubits and multiplexed photon routing reduce the effective memory lifetime requirements. This approach enhances loss tolerance, enabling higher secret key rates and secure key distribution over longer distances compared to conventional single-photon protocols. Using the Lo-Chau EPR-QKD framework and Shor-Preskill reduction, we prove that the protocol is secure without trusting intermediate nodes, making it suitable for quantum networks with untrusted repeaters.

item.title: [1★] Deterministic and Programmable Fusion for Scalable Generation of Photonic Graph States
item.author: Yan Li, ..., Hongyi Zhang, Luming Duan
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Yan Li, ..., Hongyi Zhang, Luming Duan

arXiv ID: 2610.19927 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Entanglement in multiphoton graph states is an important resource with various applications, such as measurement-based quantum computing and memory-less quantum repeaters. While some primitive instances have been successfully prepared, scalable generation of large-scale graph states with programmable connections remains an outstanding challenge. Fusion provides a promising "divide-and-conquer" approach by linking smaller resource states into larger, more complex graphs. However, its practical scalability has been limited by the probabilistic nature of conventional fusion protocols, which necessitates extensive hardware overhead and feed-forward resources to achieve deterministic outcomes. Here, we introduce and experimentally demonstrate a deterministic fusion operation with built-in error mitigation, capable of connecting small time-bin-encoded cluster states--originally generated on-demand from a quantum emitter--into larger, reconfigurable photonic graph states of increased sizes. The fusion operation is realized by nondestructively projecting pairs of flying microwave photonic qubits into Bell states using superconducting circuits with in-situ programmability. Crucially, the protocol features active reset and reuse of matter qubits during graph state generation, thereby circumventing the coherence constraints of the quantum emitter and enabling the generation of genuine multipartite entanglement across 13 photonic qubits. Our results establish a scalable framework for photonic graph-state synthesis, paving the way for fault-tolerant measurement-based quantum computation and distributed quantum networks.

Yan Li, ..., Hongyi Zhang, Luming Duan

item.title: [1★] On the structure of low-rank PPT entangled states violating Peres conjecture
item.author: Gurvir Singh, Manik Banik
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Gurvir Singh, Manik Banik

arXiv ID: 2610.19905 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Bound-entangled states with positive partial transpose (PPT) can exhibit quantum steering and Bell nonlocality, disproving the long-standing Peres conjecture and its stronger steering counterpart. These counterexamples, obtained through explicit constructions or numerical searches, raise the question of whether they share a common structural origin. We address this question in the low-rank regime by asking whether known counterexamples can be obtained, up to invertible local filtering, from the complement of an unextendible product basis (UPB). We find that the answer depends crucially on the local dimension. In 3⊗33\otimes3, the rank-four structure of PPT entangled states implies that both the steerable PPT state of Moroder \textitet al. and the Bell-nonlocal PPT state of Vértesi and Brunner can be obtained from UPB-complement states under invertible local filtering. For three qubits, in contrast, rank-four states that are PPT across every bipartition are separable across each cut. Moreover, comparison of the product-vector structure of the relevant kernels shows that the known three-qubit Bell-nonlocal PPT states cannot be obtained by invertible local filtering from the complement of any three-qubit UPB. Going beyond rank four, we further show that a known rank-eight three-qutrit state, supported on the complement of a UPB and PPT across every bipartition, is genuinely multipartite entangled. These results show that UPBs provide a unifying structural origin for important low-rank PPT entangled states in 3⊗33\otimes3, but that nonlocal bound entanglement is not, in general, a UPB phenomenon.

Gurvir Singh, Manik Banik

item.title: [1★] Trading energy for coherence in mode discrimination
item.author: Shuyang Meng, Valerio Scarani
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Shuyang Meng, Valerio Scarani

arXiv ID: 2610.19897 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Energy is arguably the main resource in classical physics; coherence is the prototypical quantum resource. In this paper, we study the interplay between these two resources in the task of optimal mode discrimination. This task, motivated by cryptography and metrology, consists of finding in which mode a signal has been encoded, for a given finite set of possible modes. After recalling that the task can be cast as a semi-definite program, we solve completely the case of two-mode discrimination under a hard energy constraint n≤Nn\leq N. Specifically, we identify the region of modes overlap, for which the maximal energy state (the Fock state with N excitations) is the best choice for discrimination. For other overlaps, having access to coherence leads to better discrimination.

Shuyang Meng, Valerio Scarani

item.title: [1★] Void-Free Through-Glass Vias for Multilayer Surface-Electrode Ion Traps
item.author: Eike Iseke, ..., Marlon Kuhn, Christian Ospelkaus
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Eike Iseke, ..., Marlon Kuhn, Christian Ospelkaus

arXiv ID: 2610.19736 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Through-substrate interconnects are a key technology for scaling surface-electrode ion traps (SEITs) toward large electrode counts and complex architectures. Dielectric substrates such as fused silica offer superior RF performance compared to silicon, but the reliable fabrication of void-free through-glass vias (TGVs) remains challenging. In this work, we demonstrate a SEIT fabricated on a fused silica substrate incorporating TGVs. The via-holes are formed using Selective Laser-Induced Etching and subsequently metallized with gold by electroplating. A patent-pending geometry-assisted bottom-up plating approach enables void-free filling using constant-current electroplating without electrolyte additives or pulsed deposition schemes. Electrical characterization across multiple wafers confirms a TGV-level yield above 98.8 %, demonstrating the robustness and reproducibility of the developed TGV technology. The TGVs are combined with multilayer SEIT fabrication, enabling vertical signal routing to all electrodes while maintaining an unaffected trapping surface without wire bonds. To interface the trap with external control electronics, a glass interposer providing signal fan-out to a larger pitch is designed and fabricated. The trap chip and the interposer are integrated using thermocompression bonding, forming a compact chip-to-chip assembly. The presented technology demonstrates the first fully integrated multilayer SEIT on fused silica incorporating void-free TGVs.

Eike Iseke, ..., Marlon Kuhn, Christian Ospelkaus

item.title: [1★] A Reconstruction of Michelson Interference from On--Off Detection Statistics
item.author: Kim Myung-Whun
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Kim Myung-Whun

arXiv ID: 2610.19569 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

This paper reconstructs the Michelson interference phenomenon based solely on the binary (on-off) statistics of a single-photon counter and macroscopic path-difference data, without the a priori assumptions of complex wave superposition or prior spectral information. In contrast to the conventional approach that assumes light as a continuous complex wave function and considers interference between them, this study focuses on the algebraic properties inherent in discrete detection statistics. We verify that the discrete response data collected across various path differences form a positive semi-definite matrix, and apply Herglotz's theorem to this result. Consequently, we show that the harmonic form of the interference fringe is not a consequence of adopting a wave model as an axiom, but rather it is uniquely decomposed into a cosine average of wavenumbers dictated by testable algebraic constraints satisfied by the statistical data. Through this approach, the logical basis of the interference phenomenon can be described by the characteristics of the binary data itself, perfectly aligning with the modern optical experimental environment that relies entirely on discrete event statistics.

Kim Myung-Whun

item.author: Achraf Boussahi
item.content:encoded:

Authors: Achraf Boussahi

arXiv ID: 2610.19544 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Pauli correlation encoding (PCE) encodes mm binary variables in the signs of kk-body Pauli correlators of n=O(m1/k)n=O(m^{1/k}) qubits, and trains a parameterized circuit on a relaxed loss of sharpness α\alpha. The strongest published schedules sharpen this loss aggressively and are benchmarked with exact expectation values, whereas a quantum computer estimates correlators from a finite number of shots. We show that the sharpness is a hidden shot budget. Since the expected sign of a correlator estimated from SS shots, erf(c√S/2)\mathrm{erf}(c\sqrt{S/2}), agrees with tanh(0.851√Sc)\tanh(0.851\sqrt{S}\,c) to within 0.0190.019, the edge term of the relaxed loss at α=0.851√S\alpha=0.851\sqrt{S} approximately equals, up to a constant, minus twice the cut expected from decoding SS shots. This explains why schedules tuned with exact expectation values lose their advantage at realistic budgets, and yields a shot-aware schedule whose final sharpness is set by the shot budget. On five G-set graphs with 800800 variables on 1313 qubits, this schedule outperforms every published schedule at its target budget in all 150150 paired comparisons of the decoded circuit output, owing to the sharpness at 1.6×1041.6\times10^4 shots and mostly to switching off the regularization at 10310^3; after a classical bit-swap search, it remains the best on average at 1.6×1041.6\times10^4 shots. Device noise damps the correlators by a factor ss, which amounts to a smaller shot budget s2Ss^2S. On the IBM Heron processor ibm_fez, an all-to-all ansatz of the type used for the best published G-set results compiles to 835835 CZ gates and decodes to a random cut, while our 9696-CZ hardware-native circuit, trained in simulation and sharpened to α≃0.65s√S\alpha\simeq0.65\,s\sqrt{S}, retains up to 0.9190.919 of the best-known cut. For new circuits, a damping and an offset calibrated on other circuits of the same graph predicted the decoded cuts at 10310^3 shots to within 0.0020.002.

item.title: [1★] Mutual Information of Measurement in Conformal Field Theories
item.author: Israel Klich, Ravisankar Rajagopal, Diana Vaman
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Israel Klich, Ravisankar Rajagopal, Diana Vaman

arXiv ID: 2610.19286 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

The mutual information of measurement of a local operator between two spatial regions characterizes the reduction in the uncertainty of measurement outcomes in one region given the outcome in the other. We study the Rényi-Shannon mutual information of measurement in conformal field theories (CFTs). Explicit calculations for scalar primaries and descendants in large NN CFTs are performed in the two extreme limits of the intervals being adjacent or largely separated. The results depend on only the cross ratio and the scaling dimension Δ\Delta of the operator being measured, with striking similarities to the mutual information of entanglement. We find a surprising quadratic dependence as (Δ−1/2)2(\Delta-1/2)^2 for adjacent intervals. This dependence superficially seems to violate the information processing inequality, which we discuss and resolve. We also offer a holographic interpretation of the mutual information of measurement.

Israel Klich, Ravisankar Rajagopal, Diana Vaman

item.title: [1★] Stabilizer Rényi Entropy Without a Phase Reference
item.author: Jinwei Chu, Savan Kharel
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Jinwei Chu, Savan Kharel

arXiv ID: 2610.18955 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Stabilizer Rényi entropy quantifies magic relative to a complete Pauli frame. In settings such as helicity states of massless particles, unsynchronized qubit registers, energy eigenbases, and systems under superselection rules, the computational basis may be fixed while the transverse Pauli axes remain unspecified. The stabilizer Rényi entropy then depends on the choice of those axes. We define a phase-averaged stabilizer Rényi entropy by averaging the Pauli moments before taking the logarithm. It is exactly invariant under independent local rephasings. For pure states, it vanishes precisely when the state is a stabilizer state in every phase convention. For a broad class of sparse supports, it reduces to a closed-form function of the basis-state probabilities alone. Within this class, the ceiling for nn channels is ln[n3/(6n−5)]\ln[n^{3}/(6n-5)] for n≥3n\geq3 and ln75\ln\frac{7}{5} for two channels. We apply the invariant to tree-level gluon scattering at four and five points, where the helicity-basis phases are unspecified. It saturates the two- and three-channel ceilings: ln75\ln\frac{7}{5} at four points and ln2713\ln\frac{27}{13} in 3→23\to2 scattering. In same-helicity 2→32\to3 scattering, it lies between a floor of ln87\ln\frac{8}{7} and a ceiling of ln184125\ln\frac{184}{125}, reached in the resolved soft limit and particular collinear limits, respectively. In every configuration studied, the invariant is independent of the fixed external colors.

Jinwei Chu, Savan Kharel

item.title: [1★] Stabilizer entropy cones as self-dual slices of linear rank cones: a five-party gap and dependence on the local dimension
item.author: Xidan Song, Ruifeng Cao
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Xidan Song, Ruifeng Cao

arXiv ID: 2610.18905 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Entanglement entropies of multipartite pure states satisfy linear inequalities; for stabilizer states, the backbone of quantum error correction, the achievable entropy vectors generate a convex cone. We show that, after a linear lift, the closure of this cone is exactly the self-dual slice of a classical object on one more element than there are parties: the closed cone generated by the rank functions of arrangements of subspaces over GF(d)\mathrm{GF}(d) for a prime local dimension dd, and of subgroups of abelian groups of exponent dividing dd in general. This correspondence brings two features of rank inequalities into play. First, the purifier acts as an extra variable: already for five parties the stabilizer cone is strictly smaller than the quantum linear rank cone, with which earlier evidence suggested it might coincide; an explicit six-variable inequality witnesses the gap. Second, the characteristic of the field enters, so the cone depends on the local dimension. It does not for up to four parties. With enough parties, the cone of Zd\mathbb{Z}_d qudits is contained in that of Zd′\mathbb{Z}_{d'} qudits if and only if dd divides d′d', and already for six parties the logical zero state of Steane's code lies outside the stabilizer cone of every odd local dimension. For this last result we show that the seven-variable characteristic-dependent inequalities we checked all follow from Shannon inequalities on the self-dual slice, and instead transfer one of them through a family of subgroups derived from the Fano plane.

Xidan Song, Ruifeng Cao

item.title: [0★] Quantum-Aware Key Rank for Side-Channel Attacks evaluation
item.author: Yevgen Kotukh
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 0 ★

Authors: Yevgen Kotukh

arXiv ID: 2610.20537 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Side-channel attacks on block ciphers rarely recover the key outright: they leave a residual key space ordered by subkey posteriors, and evaluation laboratories report the key rank of the true key against thresholds near 2^48 and 2^60. No evaluation framework models an adversary who collects traces classically and finishes the search on a quantum computer, although quantum search with advice provides exactly that. We give such an adversary a cost model and a metric. For a device whose key has rank r, any quantum algorithm with classical access to the posteriors needs Omega(sqrt(r)) cipher evaluations, and block search achieves O(sqrt(r)); the per-instance advantage is exactly quadratic, and the super-quadratic exponents reported for search with advice are averages over the prior that apply to no single device. Under the NIST MAXDEPTH budget D and a Grover iteration of g gates and depth d, the quadratic advantage holds only for ranks up to (4D/(pi d))^2 and collapses to a constant factor beyond; with the best published AES-128 oracle and D = 2^40 the window closes near rank 2^58.6. We define the quantum-aware key rank, the classical rank of equal cost, computable from the rank estimators laboratories already run, and derive the classical rank a device must retain to keep a given threshold against each depth budget. Block search and amplitude amplification from the product-form posterior state are within a factor of two to four of each other on Hamming-weight posteriors, so the cost of coherent indexing decides between them. Experiments on simulated leakage and a toy cipher confirm the predicted window: at SNR 0.125 a depth-limited quantum adversary is worth about 22 traces to a classical one, however large its gate budget.

Yevgen Kotukh

item.title: [0★] Intermediate memory costs of quantum channel synthesis with a protected subsystem
item.author: Kai Liu, Deguang Han
item.content:encoded:

Authors: Kai Liu, Deguang Han

arXiv ID: 2610.20536 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

A quantum memory can preserve a subsystem perfectly while discarding information needed by a later operation. We study the total intermediate dimension required for channel synthesis when the first stage protects a bb-dimensional subsystem and has a prescribed noncommutative graph imposing full confusability on an aa-dimensional control register. For a finite family of classically controlled branches, exact synthesis is possible if and only if the target graph contains the prescribed graph of the first stage. For every feasible family, we construct a single processor that implements all branches exactly. The processor uses pairwise nonorthogonal pure program states in a register of dimension at most aa. A target graph may be realizable with a carrier of dimension bb, while synthesizing a channel with that graph can require dimension abab. We also characterize the closure of the attainable channels, distinguishing exact synthesis from arbitrarily accurate approximation. Finally, for a family built from the trine communication task, a four-dimensional carrier permits exact synthesis with quantum programs under output depolarization. At the same total carrier dimension and without free shared randomness, classical programs have optimal normalized diamond error (1−η)/4(1-\eta)/4, where 0≤η≤10\leq\eta\leq1 is the depolarization strength. For η<1\eta<1, the gap persists under sufficiently small perturbations of the target branches.

item.author: Silas R. Beane, Roland C. Farrell, Cameron P. Shotwell
item.content:encoded:

Authors: Silas R. Beane, Roland C. Farrell, Cameron P. Shotwell

arXiv ID: 2610.20434 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

At zero temperature, a dilute Fermi gas with an attractive contact interaction forms a superfluid with gapped fermionic excitations. We show that the gap at weak coupling can be organized as a trans-series expansion in the interaction strength and the asymptotic Gor'kov-Melik-Barkhudarov gap. Abstract:

Hong-Ou-Mandel (HOM) interference offers robustness in high-noise environments due to its phase-insensitive nature, while N00N-state interference provides enhanced phase sensitivity for precision measurements in low-noise settings. This tunability enables operation in phase-insensitive, phase-sensitive, or hybrid modes within a unified setup, as confirmed by theoretical analysis and experimental demonstration. item.title: [0★] Geometric-resource bounds and permutation-averaged success probabilities for the WZP algorithm
item.author: Linlin Ye, ..., Zhaoqi Wu, Shao-Ming Fei
item.content:encoded:

Authors: Linlin Ye, ..., Zhaoqi Wu, Shao-Ming Fei

arXiv ID: 2610.20198 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Solving linear systems of equations is a fundamental task in machine learning and optimization. In this work, we extend the original WZP algorithm from real symmetric linear systems to complex Hermitian linear systems. We then study the success probability of the modified WZP algorithm from a resource-theoretic perspective. By expressing the postselection success probability as the expectation value of a positive operator, we derive upper and lower bounds of the maximal success probability over separable, incoherent, and real pure states. These bounds further establish connections between the maximal success probability and geometric entanglement, coherence, and imaginarity. We further show that, under permutation averaging, the averaged success probability is an affine function of the coherence fraction, with its dependence determined by the alignment between the success operator and the equal-superposition state. We also investigate the preprocessed WZP algorithm under subgroup-constrained preprocessing. For the two-level family, the optimal success probability is determined by the maximal projection weight onto the orbit of the target projector. Our results provide a unified perspective on the WZP success probability under different operational constraints.

Abstract:

We revisit the effective radial Schrödinger equation for a charged spinless particle in collinear static electric and magnetic fields that was formulated in our earlier work within the tridiagonal representation approach (TRA). In that model the angular factor of the electric coupling is replaced by the orientation parameter C=cosθC=\cos\theta, the linear Zeeman term is diagonal in the azimuthal quantum number, and the effective field-modified central potential takes the form V(r)=\Vt(r)+qECrV(r)=\Vt(r)+qECr. Here we show that the same equation can be solved exactly without the TRA, by the Nikiforov--Uvarov (NU) method, once the potential component \Vt(r)\Vt(r) is prescribed. Three examples are worked out in closed form: a Kratzer-type component, which yields a linear-plus-Coulomb-plus-inverse-square central potential; a pseudoharmonic-type component, which yields a linear-plus-harmonic-plus-inverse-square potential; and a Hulthén-type component with a repulsive core (Manning--Rosen form), which yields a screened confining potential with a finite number of ss-wave bound states. item.author: Fartash Chalangari, ..., Joonas Keski-Rahkonen, Esa Räsänen

Authors: Fartash Chalangari, ..., Joonas Keski-Rahkonen, Esa Räsänen

arXiv ID: 2610.20152 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We demonstrate that a single repulsive impurity enhances directional confinement of a high-energy wavepacket in a finite two-dimensional lattice of quantum wells. At energies far above the interwell barriers, the impurity suppresses transverse dynamical tunneling while preserving propagation along a principal lattice axis, even as the corresponding classical regular region shrinks. Confinement is strongest at impurity amplitudes comparable to the barrier height and weakens for stronger perturbations. Spectral analysis links this nonmonotonic pinning to the wavepacket's overlap with eigenstates concentrated along the launch direction, consistent with impurity-induced variational scarring. These results show that a single local defect can control quantum propagation over distances far exceeding its own spatial extent.

item.title: [0★] Directional effects of the Unruh effect on steering harvesting
item.author: Shu-Min Wu, Rui-Yang Xu, Zhihong Liu
item.content:encoded:

Authors: Shu-Min Wu, Rui-Yang Xu, Zhihong Liu

arXiv ID: 2610.20151 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We investigate directional quantum steering harvesting by two uniformly accelerated non-identical Unruh-DeWitt detectors coupled to a massless scalar field in the Minkowski vacuum. We show that the Unruh effect does not simply degrade harvested steering, but can reshape its directionality in a strongly parameter-dependent manner. At low detector energy scales, acceleration predominantly suppresses steering, whereas at higher energy scales, moderate acceleration can enhance steering and even activate an initially absent steering direction. Most strikingly, within a finite acceleration window, the Unruh effect enhances steering in one direction while simultaneously suppressing it in the opposite direction, revealing an intrinsically directional influence of relativistic acceleration. Detector non-identicality provides an additional control mechanism: a moderate energy-gap mismatch can enhance or activate one steering direction while suppressing the reverse one, whereas sufficiently large energy-gap mismatch suppresses the harvested steering. Moreover, the maximal steering asymmetry approximately marks the transition from two-way to one-way steering. Our results establish relativistic acceleration and detector non-identicality as means of controlling the strength and directionality of vacuum-harvested quantum correlations.

item.author: Tengiz Ibrayev, ..., Steven Waddy, Laura Manenti
item.content:encoded:

Authors: Tengiz Ibrayev, ..., Steven Waddy, Laura Manenti

arXiv ID: 2610.20132 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Ionizing radiation produces correlated errors in superconducting qubits, posing some challenges to quantum error correction. In addition, it causes background events in other superconducting cryogenic devices, such as kinetic inductance detectors and superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors. Cosmic muons are a component of this background that can only be partly shielded against at ground level, but can be tagged by an independent detector inside the cryostat, so that the affected data can be vetoed, or the muon tags incorporated into error correction. Abstract:

Frequency inhomogeneity can obscure the metrological advantage of squeezed spin states, making the choice of readout crucial. We study interacting spin-1/2 ensembles with static local frequency disorder and optimize a common collective readout over independent disorder realizations. Using Bayesian optimization of the full measurement-outcome distribution, we identify observables combining dipole and quadrupole operators that yield greater classical Fisher information than the optimized dipole readout considered here. For ensembles of up to 17 spins, their disorder-averaged CFI surpasses the standard quantum limit at both disorder strengths studied, including a regime where the dipole readout remains below it. For the larger ensembles studied, fixing the encoding axis to the direction that maximizes the disorder-averaged quantum Fisher information retains nearly the same performance. These results identify a route to extracting metrological information from frequency-disordered spin ensembles through the choice of collective observable.

item.author: Mykhailo Hontarenko, ..., Sergey Denisov, Karol Życzkowski

Authors: Mykhailo Hontarenko, ..., Sergey Denisov, Karol Życzkowski

arXiv ID: 2610.19261 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Generators of continuous-time quantum Markovian evolution, known as Lindblad operators, play a key role in the theory of open quantum systems. The question of how to define and characterize random Lindblad operators has attracted considerable attention in recent years. Purely dissipative random Lindbladians have been extensively studied using toolboxes of free probability and non-Hermitian random matrix theories, which helped, among other results, to uncover a characteristic lemon-like spectral support. In this work, we focus on random Lindbladians with a Hamiltonian component. We analyze three ensembles of increasing complexity, designed to illustrate the joint effects of dissipative and Hamiltonian dynamics. While the first two ensembles allow for an exact analytic treatment with standard probabilistic and free-probability methods, the generic case of independently random Hamiltonian and dissipative components requires a novel framework that combines operator-valued free probability with sequential noise averaging. For this ensemble, our approach preserves the underlying tensor-product structure of the Lindblad operator and derives a general equation for the spectral boundary. We characterize the effect of Hamiltonian-induced spectral squeezing and explain how the spectral support changes with the relative Hamiltonian strength and the rank of the dissipative component.

Abstract:

Quantum-walk algorithms can quadratically reduce the dependence of spatial search on the classical hitting time HT\mathrm{HT}. Realising this speedup using standard quantum-walk algorithms, however, requires deep coherent circuits, limiting their applicability on near-term and early fault-tolerant quantum devices. We also derive an optimal continuous depth-query trade-off for fixed-point amplitude amplification, providing a potential building block for other hybrid designs.

item.title: [0★] Selective Control and Imaging of Higgs and Goldstone Modes with a Quantum Simulator
item.author: Connie Miao, ..., Erich Mueller, Andre G. Petukhov
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 0 ★

Authors: Connie Miao, ..., Erich Mueller, Andre G. Petukhov

arXiv ID: 2610.19219 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We realize the mesoscopic Bose-Hubbard model at unit-filling on a two-dimensional array of transmon qubits and selectively excite collective modes associated with amplitude or phase fluctuations of the superfluid order parameter. We identify these modes respectively as the Higgs and Goldstone modes using complementary local observables, extracted from measuring the number of particles on each site. Modulation of the coupling between sites excites the Higgs mode, which we detect via the density of doubly occupied sites. In contrast, modulation of the local chemical potential with an appropriately chosen spatial profile excites the lowest-frequency Goldstone mode, which we detect via changes in the local density. The two modes have different symmetries and do not couple to one another. By varying the system geometry, we characterize the impact of finite system size on the evolution of both modes. In the thermodynamic limit, decay into a continuum of lower-energy excitations can obscure the Higgs response. In our mesoscopic system, however, the finite system size leads to spectral gaps and allows us to detect the Higgs mode as a coherent, long-lived excitation. Our work demonstrates how finite quantum simulators can isolate and probe physical phenomena that become difficult to resolve in the thermodynamic, large-scale limit.

Authors: Prince Frederick Kwao, ..., Edwin Barnes, Ayush Asthana

arXiv ID: 2610.19109 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Circuit depth and measurement count are the main limitations for chemical applications of the leading variational quantum algorithms on quantum computers. We show that both resource requirements can be reduced by augmenting adaptive variational quantum algorithms with post-optimization corrective techniques. We focus on two such techniques---Hamiltonian-moment Krylov subspace diagonalization and the identity-augmented quantum self-consistent equation of motion (q-sc-EOM)---applied to optimized ADAPT-VQE states without further ansatz growth or nonlinear optimization. Across molecular systems studied with up to 20 qubits, first-order Krylov correction reduces the optimized iterations (and the corresponding number of adaptive layers) needed to reach the 1.6 mEh1.6~\mathrm{m}E_h threshold by up to approximately sixfold, with a general trend toward larger reductions at higher determinant Rényi entropy. We also find measurement-cost reductions of up to approximately fortyfold using a suitable resource-cost model. Identity-augmented q-sc-EOM improves molecular potential-energy curves obtained from truncated ADAPT-VQE ansätze with limited expressivity and recovers accuracy from states produced by sampled operator ranking without additional gradient-based operator selection, providing an advantage when small pool gradients make selection measurement intensive. Together, these post-optimization corrections offer routes to improve energy accuracy and reduce adaptive circuit growth in quantum algorithms as quantum hardware advances.

item.author: Hussain Gohar
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 0 ★

Authors: Hussain Gohar

arXiv ID: 2610.19106 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Gravity from entropy (GfE) identifies its Lagrangian with the geometric quantum relative entropy (GQRE) between the spacetime metric and a metric induced by matter and curvature, treating the metric itself as a quantum operator. We extend this construction to the Tsallis, Rényi, and Sharma-Mittal families, which we call gravity from generalized entropy (GfGE), and determine their common Einstein limit, weak-field spectra, auxiliary-field formulation, and horizon entropy. The entropy choice controls the leading higher-curvature terms and additional modes. We confirm that the linearized GfE spectrum contains a healthy scalar and a Planck-scale tachyonic spin-2 ghost. We identify the conditions that remove this ghost: curvature must enter through its scalar trace, or the entropy generator must be flat to quadratic order at the identity. The latter gives exact general relativity for Tsallis at q=0q=0 and ghost-free f(R,Lm)f(R,L_m) theories for Rényi and Sharma-Mittal. On shell, the auxiliary G-field is proportional to the tensor in Wald's entropy formula. For analytic entropy functions, horizons with a single curvature scale have an area term followed by constant and inverse-area corrections. We also extend the volume-constraint cosmological constant to the full family; its leading entropy dependence is set by the scalar mass. A finite set of entropy-function derivatives controls the leading weak-curvature departures from general relativity.

arXiv ID: 2610.19083 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Interactions turn a gas into a fluid. We show that two-body loss can take their place. Correlated loss induces elastic scattering, as required by the optical theorem, which dominates at strong loss via the quantum Zeno effect. A nondegenerate gas with only two-body loss thus flows hydrodynamically, with viscosity and thermal conductivity close to those of the unitary Fermi gas. As loss heats the gas, both grow in time with a universal exponent 3/8. Unlike single-particle loss, two-body loss can engineer collisions, and hence transport, in quantum matter.

item.title: [0★] Federated Unlearning of Quantum Data via Classical Shadows
item.author: Zihao Ding, Jun Huang, Cong-cong Xing
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 0 ★

Authors: Zihao Ding, Jun Huang, Cong-cong Xing

arXiv ID: 2610.19077 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Quantum federated learning trains a quantum neural network (QNN) across nodes that hold quantum data, such as the states of quantum sensors. To forget data, unlearning methods for quantum models replay them, and federated unlearning from stored updates removes whole nodes only. Quantum data cannot be replayed, since a state is consumed when measured and cannot be cloned. We propose Shadow-based Data Erasure (SHADE), in which each node records a classical shadow of every training state, a few randomized single-qubit measurements taken at training time. The gradient and curvature of a QNN on a state are expectations of observables, so SHADE estimates them for the forget data from the shadows at any later parameters and removes their effect by a federated Newton correction. Only classical estimates cross the network. We prove that the shadow size needed for a target unlearning error grows exponentially in the size of the backward light cone of the measured observable and not in the number of qubits. In simulation with 50 nodes and on edge boards, SHADE matches the forget accuracy of retraining within 0.5 points, without replay and in under 0.2 s.

Zihao Ding, Jun Huang, Cong-cong Xing

item.author: Celina Bräutigam, Steffen J. Glaser, Dennis Huber

Authors: Celina Bräutigam, Steffen J. Glaser, Dennis Huber

arXiv ID: 2610.19054 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

A deep understanding of quantum information theory is essential for quantum science and technology. However, quantum mechanics and particularly quantum information theory suffer from a lack of intuitive images. Visualization tools offer novel perspectives on many problems in quantum physics by revealing important properties of quantum states and processes that are otherwise obscured by abstract mathematical formalisms. Here, we extend the previously established BEADS representation of pure states to the so-called generalized BEADS representation of mixed quantum states. We introduce spherical functions, so-called beads to visualize correlation structures of mixed quantum states. A recursive optimization scheme is used to obtain minimum-entanglement pure state decompositions of all subsystems of a given N-qubit state. We show how correlation function components can be decomposed into individual contributions that directly correspond to different types of correlations of mixed states. This allows us to visually characterize the total correlation, genuine n-partite entanglement, nonclassical quantum-discord-type correlations as well as classical correlations. After outlining the mathematical details relevant for constructing the representation, we examine the generalized BEADS representations for various classes of mixed states including product, classically correlated, separable but nonclassically correlated, as well as entangled states. As exemplary applications of the generalized BEADS representation, we showcase entanglement distillation and the effects of noise channels.

item.title: [0★] Programmable Polaron Models and Tomography in Trapped-Ion Quantum Simulators
item.author: Filip Marijanovic, ..., Guido Pagano, Eugene Demler
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 0 ★

Authors: Filip Marijanovic, ..., Guido Pagano, Eugene Demler

arXiv ID: 2610.18970 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Strong coupling between mobile charge carriers or excitons and lattice vibrations gives rise to polarons: quasiparticles formed by charge carriers dressed by a cloud of phonon excitations. Polaron formation determines transport properties of systems ranging from transition-metal oxides and organic semiconductors to light-harvesting complexes. In excitonic systems that admit a hard-core boson description, mapping the excitations to pseudospins provides a natural framework for studying polaron physics, including the nonperturbative regime in which hopping amplitudes, phonon energies, and coupling strengths are comparable. Here, we propose a trapped-ion blueprint for realizing spin-phonon Hamiltonians with programmable spatial coupling between excitation density and phonon displacements, encompassing local Holstein and long-range Fröhlich-type interactions. To access strongly dressed quasiparticles whose bare spectral weight is suppressed, we introduce displaced Green's functions implemented through spin-dependent phonon displacements. Their spectral response reveals the polaron band spectrum, including binding energies and phonon-excitation sidebands, while spatially resolved measurements probe the structure of the phonon dressing cloud, providing a route to polaron tomography. We further complement this spectroscopy with direct and ancilla-assisted measurements of spin-phonon correlations that track the coupled dynamics of the excitation and its environment. These approaches connect the emergent quasiparticle spectrum to the microscopic buildup of its dressing cloud, enabling controlled studies of how the spatial range of coupling shapes polaron formation and mobility.

Filip Marijanovic, ..., Guido Pagano, Eugene Demler
